title: Caregivers whose care recipient also has Alzheimer’s, dementia or another cognitive impairment (BRFSS 2025)
summary: Among caregivers who answered the follow-up question in the 27 areas that asked, 14.5% (weighted) said the person they care for also has Alzheimer’s disease, dementia or another cognitive impairment disorder: 4,630 of 32,510 answers (14.2% unweighted).

provenance.source_type: Federal telephone survey, self-report (CDC BRFSS, variable CRGVALZD)
provenance.origin: CDC Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) 2025 public-use data file and codebook, downloaded from the CDC website by DBbun (SHA-256 of the data zip: be4a9f167480b1ad788640e21d8b265660c12c87d54c121839c746f29d8fb734)
provenance.reliability: Self-reported survey; weighted percentage as published by CDC in the codebook; counts reproduced from the data file and matching the codebook.

limits: Asked only of caregivers, in 27 areas; not a national estimate.
The wording covers Alzheimer’s disease, dementia or another cognitive impairment, not dementia alone.
note: Context only. Not an input to any simulator and not computed by an AI model.
